definition: The zone of proximal development is the range in which a learner’s growth can be evaluated and supported through guided help rather than independent performance alone. In Vygotsky’s sociocultural framework, it refers to developmental potential that becomes visible when assistance or scaffolding is provided.

reasons: The packet states that dynamic assessment “evaluates learners' developmental potential through mediated support within the zone of proximal development (ZPD),” but it does not define ZPD as “the range in which a learner’s growth can be evaluated and supported.”
The definition’s contrast—“guided help rather than independent performance alone”—is not supported anywhere in the packet text.

While the packet mentions “mediated support,” it does not explicitly link ZPD to “assistance or scaffolding” in the way the definition phrases it (i.e., that developmental potential becomes visible specifically when assistance/scaffolding is provided).

The packet supports ZPD as a Vygotskian concept tied to mediated support and developmental potential, but it does not explicitly define it as a range in which growth is evaluated or as something contrasted with independent performance alone.
“Assistance or scaffolding” and “becomes visible” go beyond the packet’s wording; the packet only says developmental potential is evaluated through mediated support within the ZPD.
The definition is more expansive than the supplied source and blends in dynamic assessment language that is not itself the definition of the zone of proximal development.
